unit_attributes.scope_text: Applies to an employee of a covered employer seeking status as an eligible employee.
unit_attributes.choice_text: An eligible employee must satisfy all three criteria: (1) has been employed by the employer for at least 12 months; AND (2) has been employed for at least 1,250 hours of service during the 12-month period immediately preceding the commencement of the leave (subject to special rules for airline flight crew employees in § 825.801); AND (3) is employed at a worksite where 50 or more employees are employed by the employer within 75 miles of that worksite (referencing § 825.105(b) for employees working outside the U.S.).
unit_attributes.statement: An eligible employee is defined as an employee of a covered employer who has been employed by the employer for at least 12 months, has been employed for at least 1,250 hours of service during the 12-month period immediately preceding the commencement of the leave (noting § 825.801 for airline flight crew employees), and is employed at a worksite where 50 or more employees are employed by the employer within 75 miles of that worksite (noting § 825.105(b) regarding employees working outside the U.S.).

unit_attributes.scope_text: Applies when determining whether an employee has met the requirement to have been employed by the employer for at least 12 months, subject to the break-in-service rules of paragraph (b).
unit_attributes.statement: The 12 months an employee must have been employed by the employer need not be consecutive months, provided that the break-in-service rules of paragraph (b) are met.

unit_attributes.scope_text: Applies in determining whether an employee has been employed by the employer for at least 12 months when there is a break in service of seven years or more, subject to the exceptions provided in paragraph (b)(2) of this section.
unit_attributes.statement: Subject to the exceptions in paragraph (b)(2) of this section, employment periods prior to a break in service of seven years or more need not be counted in determining whether the employee has been employed by the employer for at least 12 months.

unit_attributes.scope_text: Applies in determining whether the employee has been employed by the employer for at least 12 months when the employee has experienced a break in service of more than seven years, where either the break was occasioned by USERRA-covered service or a written agreement exists concerning the employer's intention to rehire the employee after the break.
unit_attributes.choice_text: Employment periods preceding a break in service of more than seven years must be counted where either: (i) the employee's break in service is occasioned by the fulfillment of a USERRA-covered service obligation; OR (ii) a written agreement, including a collective bargaining agreement, exists concerning the employer's intention to rehire the employee after the break in service (e.g., for education or childrearing).
unit_attributes.statement: In determining whether an employee has been employed by the employer for at least 12 months, employment periods preceding a break in service of more than seven years must be counted where the employee's break in service is occasioned by the fulfillment of a USERRA (38 U.S.C. 4301 et seq.) covered service obligation, or where a written agreement, including a collective bargaining agreement, exists concerning the employer's intention to rehire the employee after the break in service.

unit_attributes.scope_text: Applies in determining whether the employee has been employed for at least 12 months by the employer when an absence from work is due to or necessitated by USERRA-covered service.
unit_attributes.statement: The period of absence from work due to or necessitated by USERRA-covered service must also be counted in determining whether the employee has been employed for at least 12 months by the employer, though this section does not provide any greater entitlement to the employee than would be available under USERRA.

unit_attributes.scope_text: Applies to employee entitlements under 29 CFR 825.110 in relation to USERRA.
unit_attributes.statement: This section does not provide any greater entitlement to the employee than would be available under the USERRA.

unit_attributes.scope_text: Applies whenever an employee is maintained on the payroll for any part of a week, including any periods of paid or unpaid leave (sick, vacation) during which other benefits or compensation are provided by the employer (e.g., workers' compensation, group health plan benefits).
unit_attributes.statement: If an employee is maintained on the payroll for any part of a week, including any periods of paid or unpaid leave (such as sick or vacation) during which other benefits or compensation are provided by the employer (e.g., workers' compensation, group health plan benefits, etc.), the week counts as a week of employment.

unit_attributes.scope_text: Applies for purposes of determining whether intermittent, occasional, or casual employment qualifies as at least 12 months.
unit_attributes.statement: For purposes of determining whether intermittent/occasional/casual employment qualifies as at least 12 months, 52 weeks is deemed to be equal to 12 months.

unit_attributes.scope_text: Applies when determining whether an employee has met the 12-month employment requirement.
unit_attributes.statement: Nothing in this section prevents employers from considering employment prior to a continuous break in service of more than seven years when determining whether an employee has met the 12-month employment requirement.

unit_attributes.scope_text: Applies if an employer chooses to recognize employment prior to a continuous break in service of more than seven years when determining whether an employee has met the 12-month employment requirement.
unit_attributes.statement: If an employer chooses to recognize employment prior to a continuous break in service of more than seven years, the employer must do so uniformly with respect to all employees with similar breaks in service.
